Nantucket.wildlife_intro:
Nantucket's wildlife work is shaped by two things: very old houses and a very seasonal population. In town, bats roost in the attics of whaling-era captains' houses, raccoons use chimneys along the historic streets, and Norway rats follow the harbor, restaurant, and ferry blocks. Gray squirrels and skunks are steady across the island, and in Madaket, Surfside, Cisco, and 'Sconset, seasonal homes closed for the winter regularly open to mice, squirrels, and bat colonies.

Spring opening is the island's signature season for our crew — inspections, cleanouts, and sealing before families arrive. Summer brings raccoon families and skunk dens in occupied homes. Nantucket has no coyotes or fishers to worry about, which keeps the focus on structure: keeping bats, rodents, and raccoons out of historic fabric that needs careful, preservation-minded exclusion. All work follows Massachusetts PAC rules, bats by exclusion only in the permitted May and August-to-October windows. Call us early — island scheduling fills fast in spring.

faqs.q: How much does wildlife removal cost on Nantucket?
faqs.a: Pricing depends on the animal, the age and construction of the home, and how much careful sealing the job needs — historic houses often require more detailed exclusion work. We inspect, explain the scope fully, and quote the complete job before starting. Call us to book, especially before spring opening.

faqs.q: Can bat exclusion be done without harming our historic home's exterior?
faqs.a: Yes — exclusion is designed around the building. Our crew uses one-way exits fitted at the bats' actual entry gaps, then seals those gaps with materials matched to the house once the colony has left in a permitted window. No trapping or harm to the bats, and no changes to the historic appearance of the home.
